newsitem.title: THAILAND: Siam Cement sees forex loss from weaker baht.
newsitem.headline: Siam Cement sees forex loss from weaker baht.

text.p: The Siam Cement Plc said on Thursday its consolidated earnings would be hurt by Thailand's decision to let the baht lose on a managed float last week.

The industrial and construction materials group said in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand its consolidated net profit could be eroded by 2.7 billion baht if the baht stood at 27.00 to the dollar, rising to 9.9 billion if the currency eased to 30.00.
"The Bank of Thailand's announcement last week of a managed float foreign exchange rate regime for the baht will have a significant impact on the Siam Cement Group," it said.
Siam Cement said its current outstanding $4 billion foreign debt included about $1 billion in short-term offshore loans and $3 billion in long-term borrowing.
It said part of the foreign exchange losses would be reflected on the group's second quarter financial statement due for release by end-August.
Siam Cement posted a 6.8 billion baht consolidated net profit in 1996.
